title: Attention kernel tuning cascade and stability test harness
creator: Evan Park
description: Problem: integrations of newer attention kernels (v2 and v3 variants) have produced intermittent latency spikes and memory fragmentation events during mixed prefill/decode workloads. These manifest as 99th-percentile latency regressions for decoder-heavy flows and occasional OOMs on medium-sized multitenant hosts. Scope: define a deterministic tuning cascade for kernel selection, build a stability test harness that simulates startup/backpressure/warmup patterns, and implement guarded rollout policies and rollback triggers. Goals: 1) produce a reproducible harness that can emulate realistic prefill-to-decode transitions at scale; 2) codify a kernel selection cascade that prefers stable kernels for coldstart and switches to high-throughput kernels after validated warmup; 3) add regression detection rules tied to telemetry so we can auto-fence new kernel rollouts; 4) document playbook for on-call to mitigate regressions quickly.
steps_to_reproduce: Run mixed workload benchmark: 50% short-system prompts (prefill length 512), 50% long decode tails (decode up to 1024) against a pool of 16 GPUs with mixed-precision enabled.
Start with default kernel routing that prefers v3 where available. Gradually ramp synthetic burst requests to 400 qps over 2 minutes.
Observe 99p latency, memory resident set size (RSS) variance, and kernel flip counts from telemetry.
Repeat with deterministic seed for cache evictions and with/without KV prefix caching enabled to compare outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Stability harness reproduces observed latency spikes locally and in staging with a deterministic seed >= 90% of runs.
Tuning cascade implemented: coldstart -> v2-fallback-safeguard -> v3-after-stable-warmup, configurable via deployment flags.
Telemetry alerts fire when 99p latency increases >25% or OOM frequency >0.2% for a 10-minute window during canary.
Runbook created with step-by-step rollback and mitigation actions and validated by on-call rotation in staging drill.
Benchmarks show no >10% cost regression for normal traffic after applying cascade heuristics.
notes: Design decisions considered: prefer deterministic stability over peak throughput for coldstart windows to reduce customer-visible regressions.
Trade-offs: keeping v3 gated during warmup increases token cost by ~4% on bursty traffic but reduces 99p tail by ~30ms in our staging runs.
We will surface a toggle in Dedicated config to allow tenants to opt into immediate v3 usage if they accept higher variance.
We observed a correlation between microbatch size oscillation and kernel handoff rate; the harness includes a jitter injector to validate mitigations.
